podcast.title: EP Produced by Robin Guthrie (1987)
podcast.body: In 1987, AR Kane signed with 4AD and released an EP that was produced by Robin Guthrie of the Cocteau Twins, marking a significant collaboration.

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: "The Black Jesus and Mary Chain" Comparison
podcast.body: Early in their career, AR Kane's sound was quite noisy, leading writers to compare them to The Jesus and Mary Chain, dubbing them "the Black Jesus and Mary Chain."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Coined the Term "Dreampop"
podcast.body: Alex Ayuli originated the term "Dreampop" to describe AR Kane's music. He did this as a way to challenge journalists who were assigning labels the band disliked, providing a distinct descriptor for their atmospheric and textured sound.

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Tremendous Influence
podcast.body: Although not widely known, AR Kane, composed of Alex Ayuli and Rudy Tambala, was tremendously influential across several genres, including Dreampop, Trip Hop, and Shoegaze, due to their unique musical approach.

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Acronymic Band Name
xref.body: The name M|A|R|R|S is an acronym formed from the first initials of the individuals involved in the project: Martin Young, Alex Ayuli, Rudy Tambala, Russell Smith, and Steve Young. "The name is an acronym taken from the initials of the first names of the people involved, Martin Young from Colorbox, Alex Auley from AR Kane, Rudy Tambawa also from Colorbox, Russell Smith, an associate of Colorbox, and Steve Young, another member of Colorbox."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The 50 Biggest All-Time Alt-Rock One-Hit Wonders: Part 1

xref.title: Collaboration and Formation
xref.body: MARRS formed in 1988 through a collaboration between members of AR Kane (Alex Ayuli, Rudy Tambala), Colorbox (Martin Young, Stephen Young), and Russell Smith, an associate of AR Kane. The name is an acronym of the members' initials.

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Collaborative Formation
xref.body: The group was a collaboration between two acts signed to Britain's 4AD label: AR Kane and Colorbox. "This was a one-time only project by a couple of groups on Britain's 4AD label, AR Kane and Colorbox."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
srcs.episode: The 50 Biggest All-Time Alt-Rock One-Hit Wonders: Part 1

xref.title: Comparison to AR Kane
xref.body: AR Kane was often referred to by more than one writer as "the Black Jesus and Mary Chain" due to their noisy sound in their early days, indicating a shared aesthetic with this band.

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music
